scenarios.situation: Every file in a run fails, so each row names its failure and the status bar reads zero of three cleaned.
An Arabic speaker sees the row arrow in a right-to-left layout, where it is not mirrored.
Someone scanning a large run sees a folder or file row that is closed, with the arrow pointing right.
Someone opens a row to see what was removed and the arrow turns to point down.
Someone moves the pointer over Choose files and the button background darkens.
Someone tabs to Choose files and sees a visible focus ring around the button.
Someone opens the app with Save as copy off and reads that files will be cleaned in place.
Someone drags files over the window with Save as copy off, and the prompt asks them to drop the files.
Someone opens the app with Save as copy on and reads that the originals stay unchanged.
Someone drags files over the window with Save as copy on, and the prompt asks them to drop the files.
The app opens before its settings are read, so the screen shows no line about copies or in-place cleaning.
Someone drags a file over the window before settings are read, and the prompt asks them to drop it.
Someone using German opens the app and sees the empty screen with its longer words.
Someone using Malayalam opens the app and sees the empty screen in a script with tall letters.
Someone using Persian opens the app and sees the empty screen mirrored right to left.
Someone moves the pointer over Choose folder and its border takes the accent colour.
Someone moves the pointer over Try again and the button fills with the highlight colour.
A screen fails while drawing and the guard shows a plain message with the cause and a Try again button.
A drawing failure carries a very long file path and the message wraps inside the box and does not run off the edge.
The app draws its screens as normal and the error guard stays out of the way, with no message and no logged error.
Someone tabs to the Try again button of the error message and sees a visible focus ring around it.
After a drawing failure the cause goes away, Try again is pressed and the screen comes back with the alert gone.
The cleaned copy was written but a leftover file could not be removed, and the row names its path.
Another app changed the file while it was being cleaned, so the row reports that the final step failed.
The engine stopped before it gave a verdict, so the row shows its plain message and no failure kind.
A failure carries a long leftover path, so the row detail wraps instead of running past the window edge.
A RAF file is refused because writing it can damage the original, and the row says it was left unchanged.
The cleaned copy could not be checked, so someone opens the row to read why before trusting the result.
A cleaned copy could not be written, so someone opens the row to read what failed and where the leftover file is.
Embedded metadata is gone, but macOS kept some of the file's extra data, and the row names the cleaned file.
A file with no removable metadata is left alone, and its row says the file was not rewritten.
Someone opens the row of a file with nothing to remove and reads the same plain message inside it.
A file name has Arabic words with Arabic-Indic digits, and its row shows the name without scrambling it.
A file is cleaned in place and its row shows a check, the removed verdict and the before and after counts.
Someone opens a cleaned row to read which fields were removed and which are still present.
A leftover file could not be removed after a failed check, so the row says so and names its path when it has one.
Another app changed the file while it was being cleaned, so the row says the cleaned file could not be saved over it.
Save as copy is on, so the row says it was written to a copy and the original stays as it was.
A failed file in a long run stays folded, showing only its summary, until someone opens it to read why.
The engine stopped before it gave a verdict, so the row shows its plain message and no failure summary.
A long German compound word names a file, and the row cuts it at the edge of the name cell.
A file name mixes Hebrew and Latin letters, and its row shows the name in reading order.
A file of one tebibyte shows in the size cell with the largest unit the app has.
A file with counts of six digits shows both numbers in cells built for three digits.
A long Japanese name has no spaces to wrap at, so the row cuts it at the edge of the name cell.
A file one kilobyte short of a megabyte shows how the size cell rounds at the unit edge.
A name of 180 letters with no break stays on one line in the name cell and runs out of room.
A file name mixes left-to-right and right-to-left overrides that are each closed, and the row shows it.
A name with a run of sixteen dots makes the row show where the name ends and the extension begins.
A file in a large run waits its turn, so its row shows a pending dot and no counts yet.
The app is removing metadata from a file, so its row shows a spinner while the counts stay empty.
The app is reading a file's metadata, so its row shows a spinner and no counts yet.
A RAF file is refused because writing it can damage the original, and the row says it was left unchanged.
A file name carries a right-to-left override, so its row can draw the extension in a different order.
Someone moves the pointer over a cleaned row and its background changes to the surface colour.
Someone tabs to a cleaned row and sees a visible focus ring around the whole row.
A file was rewritten but nothing measured changed, so the row says so instead of claiming a removal.
The check on a new copy failed, so the row says it could not verify it and your original is unchanged.
A cleaned copy could not be written, so the row says so and opens to the leftover file's path, with and without that path.
Embedded metadata is gone but macOS kept some extra file data, so the row says so, with and without the cleaned file's path.
A file with no bytes in it cannot be read, so the row shows an error and a size of zero.
A file with no bytes has no metadata to remove, so the row says nothing was found and shows zero.
A file name has a family emoji joined by zero width joiners, and its row keeps it as one picture.
Someone using Arabic sees a mixed batch with the table and the status bar mirrored right to left.
Someone drops a folder of two files and the table shows the folder row with its count above both files.
Someone drops a folder with nothing supported in it and the table shows its row reading zero supported files.
Someone drops a big folder and the table shows its row still scanning, with no files under it yet.
Someone using German sees a mixed batch in the table and the status bar at the default window width.
Someone moves the pointer over a column header and its label changes to the full text colour.
Someone using Hungarian sees a mixed batch in the table and the status bar at the default window width.
Someone using Japanese sees a mixed batch in the table and the status bar, with no spaces to wrap at.
A run is under way with a failed file, a waiting file and a finished file, and the rows keep the order they were added in.
Someone using Persian sees a mixed batch with the table and the status bar mirrored right to left.
Someone tabs to the Name column header and sees a visible focus ring around its sort button.
Someone sorts a finished batch by name and the rows reorder from A to Z with the column marked ascending.
Someone clicks the name column twice and the rows reorder from Z to A with the column marked descending.
Two files of the same size are sorted by size, and the table keeps the pair in the order they were added.
Someone sorts a mixed batch both ways and finished files stay above waiting ones, with failed files last.
Someone using Arabic drops a folder with an Arabic name and the row shows it in the right direction.
After a large run someone folds a folder away and its row shows a chevron pointing right with the same count.
Someone drops a folder and its row shows the folder, a chevron pointing down and how many files it holds.
The row of a folder with nothing supported is folded away at once and still reads zero supported files.
Someone drops a folder with nothing supported in it and its row reads zero supported files for a moment.
Someone tabs to the fold button of a folder row and sees a visible focus ring around it.
A folder deep in the tree shows a shortened path in the row and keeps the full path in its tooltip and name.
Someone drops a big folder and the row shows that it is still being scanned before any file count is known.
Someone drops a folder that holds exactly one supported file and its row shows a count of one.
Someone moves the pointer over the fold button of a folder row and the chevron changes to the accent colour.
Someone looks for the settings on first launch and finds the gear button labelled Open settings.
Someone points at the gear button and its colour darkens to show it can be pressed.
Someone tabs to the gear button and sees a focus ring before opening the settings.
With the settings drawer showing, the gear button is labelled Close settings so it can be shut again.
Someone moves the pointer down the open list and each item under it takes the highlight, the same one the arrow keys set.
Someone presses End in the open list and the focus jumps to the last language and scrolls it into view.
Someone tabs to the closed language trigger and sees a visible focus ring around it.
Someone opens the list with the arrow keys, moves down two items and presses Enter to choose that language.
Someone opens the language list and sees System and every language in its own script, each with its English name.
Someone who chose German opens the list and sees a check mark and the accent colour on that one language.
Someone using Arabic or Persian sees the language list laid out right to left.
Someone opens the language list with the app following the system language.
Someone moves the pointer over the language trigger and its border darkens.
A saved language code that the list no longer knows shows on the trigger as the raw code and not as a name.
Someone opens a cleaned photo and reads that all five fields were removed, with no list of kept fields to open.
An Arabic speaker opens a cleaned file with two fields removed and reads the count from the general plural wording.
Someone points at Copy all and its background changes to show it can be pressed.
Someone tabs to Copy all and sees a focus ring before copying the list.
Someone opens a cleaned file and reads two fields removed and one still present, with the removed ones listed under their group.
Someone opens a cleaned file that only carried file-system fields, so the panel says No metadata found and offers nothing to copy.
Someone opens a file where one field was removed and reads the singular wording.
Someone opens the still present list to check which fields the cleaned file kept.
Someone opens a file with thirty camera settings and scrolls the list inside a panel that stops growing at 300 pixels.
Someone opens a file whose cleaning changed nothing and reads 0 fields removed with its one field still present.
Someone reads an office name that mixes Arabic and Latin letters and finds each part in its own reading direction.
Someone reads a description of 81 characters that is cut after 80 with an ellipsis, and finds the full text by pointing at it.
Someone reads a description of exactly 80 characters, which shows in full with no ellipsis.
Someone reads a removed field marked with a minus and a kept field marked with a check, each with its value.
Someone reads a removed location field whose value is a list of two numbers, shown as its plain text.
Someone sees a Camera group that holds six removed fields and its count of 6.
Someone sees a Camera group that holds one removed field and its count of 1.
Someone sees a group the app has no name for under the heading Other, and can point at it to read the real group name.
An Arabic speaker reads the three appearance segments in a right-to-left layout.
Someone picks the Dark appearance and sees that segment chosen while the others stay unselected.
Someone tabs to the appearance control and sees a focus ring on the chosen segment.
Someone presses the right arrow on the last segment and the choice wraps to the first one.
Someone opens the app for the first time and sees the Light appearance as the chosen segment.
A Russian speaker sees the longest translated segment labels still fit inside the control.
Someone leaves the appearance on Auto and sees that segment chosen, the default for a first launch.
A folder run ends and the bar reads three of three cleaned with the fields removed and a Clear button to start again.
Someone using Arabic sees the counts, the time and the Clear button of the bar laid out right to left.
Someone opens the app with no file yet and the bottom bar shows only the settings gear, with no counts.
Someone tabs from the settings gear to the Clear button of the bar and sees a visible focus ring on each stop.
Partway through a run the bar shows one of three cleaned, the fields removed so far and the seconds passed.
Files that were already clean give zero of twelve cleaned and zero fields removed, so the zero reads as a result and not a gap.
A large run has begun and the bar reads zero of three cleaned with no time passed.
Someone cleans a single file and the bar reads one of one cleaned with a count of one field removed.
A file is finished and shows a check, and a file with no metadata found shows the same check.
The first file finishes in front of the person and its check draws itself in once.
A file could not be cleaned and its row shows a red cross announced as an error.
A failed file's cross is announced with the reason for the failure rather than the word error.
A file in a big drop is waiting its turn and shows a small grey dot until it is picked up.
A file is being read or cleaned and shows a spinner, and a file still being read looks the same.
An Arabic speaker copies the list and the confirmation notice appears in Arabic in a right-to-left layout.
Someone copies the removed-metadata list and a short notice confirms the text is on the clipboard.
The notice timer runs out, so the message is still set but the notice has faded away.
Nothing has been copied or skipped, so the notice holds no text and stays out of sight.
In the narrow default window the longest translated skipped notice wraps inside the window width.
Someone reveals a result that was moved or deleted after its row appeared and is told it no longer exists.
A drop contains several unsupported files and the notice says how many were skipped.
A drop contains a single unsupported file and the notice reports the one that was skipped.
An Arabic speaker reads a setting in a right-to-left layout with its label and description in Arabic.
Someone tabs to a setting with the keyboard and sees a focus ring on the switch before changing it.
A Spanish speaker opens the settings and the longest translated label and description still fit beside the switch.
Someone leaves a setting off before sharing a file and can see from the switch and its label that it is not applied.
Someone turns on Save as copy so the original is kept exactly as it was, and reads the setting description.
Someone checks a cleaned phone photo and sees its type as a HEIC or HEIF badge in one colour.
Someone checks a cleaned photo and sees its type as a JPG or JPEG badge in one colour.
A folder of recordings is cleaned and every audio and video type shows the same media colour.
A mixed folder is cleaned and the supported types with no colour of their own show a plain badge.
Someone checks a cleaned document and sees its type as a PDF badge in its own colour.
Someone checks a cleaned screenshot and sees its type as a PNG badge in its own colour.
Someone checks cleaned camera files and every RAW type, from DNG to SRW, shows the same colour.
